AH02.title: Worker submits an asset -> it enters the pending queue
AH02.notes: FIXTURE BUILT, THEN WALKED 2026-07-28. The blocker was real and it was in the SEEDER hand-off: assets.py computes auth_uid from the submitter but builds ctx in memory only, and asset_brain.py - which does the actual asset_nodes insert - DROPPED auth_uid from its row mapping and hardcoded status='approved'. Two omissions, and between them the page's whole governance workflow was untestable: 95 rows, 0 with an author, 0 pending, 0 rejected. Fixed at the source (_governance_state generates the status and its companion fields TOGETHER so a pending row cannot claim a reviewer and a rejected row cannot lack a reason - the PM9 coherence lesson), and auth_uid is now carried through. Verified over 400 draws: 82/12/6 approved/pending/rejected, ZERO internally inconsistent rows. Applied to the live fixture too: 79 approved / 12 pending / 4 rejected, authors attached (5 approved rows keep no author because they had no submitted_by to resolve - recorded, not hidden).

AH03.title: Supervisor approves / rejects - and the rejection must SAY WHY
AH03.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 and found a REAL authority hole - the first thing the new fixture made visible. THE GOOD HALF FIRST: wh_guard_supervisor_approval is a well-built generic trigger (SECURITY DEFINER, six tables, service_role exempt) and it correctly refuses a non-supervisor who APPROVES - a worker approving their own pending asset is rejected 42501 with a message naming the user and hive. That is the opposite of the PM arc's pattern and stays exactly as it is. THE HOLE: its UPDATE clause treated a status change as privileged only when 'approved' was on one side, so pending -> rejected slipped through. ('rejected' does appear in sup_states, but that array is only consulted for the wo_state column.) Probed live: a WORKER set their own pending asset to 'rejected' AND wrote rejection_reason = 'Rejected by the supervisor - not fit for the register.' One row, no error. REACHABLE, not theoretical: asset-hub's own reject is caught only INCIDENTALLY, because it also writes approved_by/approved_at and the guard notices those. hive.html's rejectItem() updates { status: 'rejected' } ALONE, behind a client-side role check - PMK6's class on the approval queue. WHY THE REASON FIELD IS THE SHARP PART: rejection_reason is the REVIEWER'S VOICE. The queue renders it back to the submitter as 'Why: ...' and the PDDA arc added it precisely so a rejection would explain itself. A submitter who can write it authors a verdict in a supervisor's name, and the next supervisor reading the queue cannot tell. FIXED centrally in migration 20260728000013 - one clause, SIX tables, because every approval queue on the platform shared the hole. Safe to tighten, measured first: both legitimate reject paths are already supervisor-only in their UI and service_role is exempt. Proven: worker self-reject BLOCKED, worker editing the reason alone BLOCKED, supervisor reject still 1 row. GATED by tools/validate_approval_authority.py (registered); teeth proven against the REAL pre-fix guard - 3 of 4 checks fail, exit 1.

AH04.title: Restore a rejected asset - can the submitter see what happened?
AH04.notes: G partial and BLOCKED ON A FIXTURE, measured 2026-07-28: asset_nodes has 95 rows, ALL seeder-created (auth_uid NULL on every one), ALL status='approved', ZERO pending and ZERO rejected, and 0 rows authored by any worker or supervisor. rcm_strategies is 172 approved / 0 unapproved. So the submit -> review -> approve/reject -> restore workflow has no data in any state but the terminal one, which is exactly why the PDDA arc's F21 (a worker's Pending-assets tile always reads 0) was never diagnosed - there has never been a pending asset to see. The fixture, not the walker, is the binding constraint (LB13/LB17 again).

AH08.title: RCM strategy -> interval -> push to PM Scheduler
AH08.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28, after building the TWO fixture states it needed - and the fixture work is the finding. (1) rcm_strategies was 172 approved / 0 unapproved, because reliability.py set approved_by/approved_at UNCONDITIONALLY while the fmea_modes rows twelve lines above already had an is_approved branch (245 of 300). Same file, adjacent tables, one walkable and one not. It matters because pushStrategyToPm() refuses an unapproved strategy - 'Strategy must be approved before pushing to PM Scheduler' - so with no unapproved rows in existence that REFUSAL had never once been exercised; the guard could have been inverted or dead and nothing would have shown it. Fixed to mirror the FMEA branch, coherently (an unapproved strategy has NEITHER an approver nor a timestamp). Live: 146 approved / 26 unapproved. (2) 0 of 172 strategies were linked to a PM scope item. RECALLING THE DISPOSITION stopped this being filed as a bug: the seeder comment calls the unlinked state 'the realistic cold-start state', and that is right. But with EVERY row cold-start the linked branch was undemonstrable - pushStrategyToPm's idempotence guard ('Already linked to PM Scheduler') and the written_to_pm_scope_item_id FK had no row to protect. That is the logbook arc's LB13 exactly. Resolved the same way: seed a SAMPLE so BOTH branches exist without pretending every plant has finished its RCM roll-out. Live: 21 of 172 linked, 0 dangling. THE CORRECTNESS RESULT: no pushed scope item is scheduled RARER than its strategy specifies (0 of 21), none sits in a different hive from its strategy, and the pairs are exact - 30d->Monthly, 90d->Quarterly, 180d->Semi-Annual. That property does not rest on the fixture: only 3 distinct intervals exist in the data (30/90/180, all canonical buckets), so the mapping is barely exercised here - it holds for ARBITRARY intervals because validate_pm_frequency_mapping proves never-rarer across 1..400, the PMK4 gate from the PM arc. A MISTAKE OF MY OWN, caught and undone: my first bulk link paired rows by two unrelated row_number() orderings, so 18 of 21 strategies got ANOTHER strategy's scope item (a 30-day strategy pointing at a Semi-Annual task). Caught by verifying the pairing rather than the row count, fully reverted (links cleared, the 21 wrong scope items deleted, 0 completions orphaned), and redone one row at a time so an insert cannot drift from its strategy. The seeder helper already inserts per-row and never had the bug. Compliance moved 86.3 -> 85.2 as the 21 new scope items entered the scheduled denominator with no completions yet; the on-time gap NARROWED 13.3 -> 12.2, so the forward-only ratchet passed and was re-accepted at the tighter ceiling.

AH09.title: Weibull fit - with too few failures, does it refuse or guess?
AH09.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THE ENGINE'S REFUSAL PATH IS EXCELLENT AND STAYS - recorded as a real result, because the arc's premise (AHK2) half-expected it to be missing. python-api/reliability/weibull.py sets MIN_FAILURES_FOR_FIT=4 and below it attempts NO fit: beta NULL, eta NULL, failure_pattern='insufficient_data', plus a degenerate-likelihood guard for all-identical durations. That is why min(n_failures) across 91 fits is exactly 4 - nothing weaker ever gets a number. It also writes an ACTIONABLE diagnostic: 'Need at least 4 corrective events in the lookback window (have 2). Log more breakdowns or widen since_days before refitting.' THE DEFECT IS THAT THE SENTENCE COULD ONLY EVER BE SEEN ONCE. weibull_fits had no diagnostic column, so persistFit never wrote it, v_weibull_truth could not expose it, and loadLatestWeibull selected a column set that could not contain it - fit.diagnostic was undefined and diagEl.textContent = fit.diagnostic || '' cleared the box. Visible for a few seconds after Compute; blank on every load after that. What a planner opening the asset the next day saw: beta '--', eta '--', a pill reading 'insufficient data', and an EMPTY bordered box where the explanation belongs. The number is correctly absent and the REASON is silently absent too - the F18 dead-card shape landing on the most important sentence in the reliability workbench. FIXED as ONE definition rather than two: the engine already writes the sentence, so persist what it wrote (migration 20260728000014 adds the column and re-exposes the view; the fitter writes it; the page selects it on the LOAD path). Re-deriving the wording client-side would have put the same sentence in two places and let them drift - the logbook arc's three-ways-to-say-'corrective'. A NEAR-MISS OF MY OWN, caught by reading before rewriting: v_weibull_truth is NOT a plain projection - it is DISTINCT ON (hive_id, asset_id, COALESCE(fmea_mode_id,'_')) ORDER BY generated_at DESC, which is what makes it the LATEST fit per asset, and it aliases id AS fit_id. My first migration draft recreated it from the column list alone, which would have silently handed every consumer the FULL fit history and renamed a column. Caught by dumping the real definition first; the gate now asserts the DISTINCT ON survives. AND ONE MORE INSTRUMENT ERROR: my post-migration leak check ran as the postgres superuser (BYPASSRLS) and reported 'LEAK'. Re-run as a real authenticated member: 1 hive visible, 31 rows, no leak. VERIFIED LIVE on a page LOAD (not the compute path): beta '--', eta '--', pattern 'insufficient data', meta 'n_failures 2 - n_censored 1 - window 365d', and the diagnostic now reads in full. GATED by tools/validate_refusal_reason_persists.py (registered), which holds the whole round-trip because breaking any link restores the silent blank; teeth proven twice - reverting the page select and dropping the column each give exit 1.

AH10.title: P-F interval - the number that sets inspection frequency
AH10.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 - CLEAN, with one measured asymmetry recorded rather than migrated away. The P-F engine refuses properly, with FOUR distinct diagnostics (fewer than 2 valid readings, no detectable P-F pair, and two degenerate cases), and the compute path COMMUNICATES the refusal: #pf-status shows data.diagnostic and the toast says 'No P-F pair detected, see diagnostic.' So unlike AH9, the user is told why at the moment it happens. THE ASYMMETRY, and its cause measured rather than assumed: a P-F refusal has NO ROW AT ALL, so its reason cannot survive a reload the way weibull_fits.diagnostic now does. Verified live on the SAME asset - the Weibull card reads 'insufficient data' with its full reason, while the P-F panel shows only its first-run copy. AND THE STATED REASON WAS WRONG IN BOTH COMMENTS. python-api/reliability/pf_interval.py and supabase/functions/pf-calculator/index.ts each said refusals are not persisted 'because pf_intervals.pf_days has a CHECK > 0'. That is not the blocker: in SQL `NULL > 0` evaluates to NULL and a CHECK treats NULL as SATISFIED, so the CHECK would happily accept a NULL. Probed it - the insert fails 23502, the NOT NULL constraint. The distinction is load-bearing for the next reader: someone relaxing the CHECK to persist refusals would find them still rejected and not know why. Both comments corrected to name the real constraint and to record the consequence. NOT MIGRATED, deliberately: making pf_days nullable to store refusals would weaken a column whose not-nullness is what guarantees every stored P-F row HAS a window - the same reasoning that kept get_pm_compliance_smrp intact in the PM arc. The first-run copy is also correct guidance in the state where it actually appears (this asset has never had a P-F computed); it only reads oddly in the seconds right after a refusal, where #pf-status carries the truth directly beneath it. Recorded as a low-severity nit, not a defect. FMEA RPN is the remaining third of AHK2 and needs a DIFFERENT question - it is arithmetic on three 1-10 inputs, so the issue is whether the inputs are defensible, not whether the product is.

AHK1.name: A governance decision needs an IDENTITY, not a name
AHK1.notes: OPEN on measured evidence (2026-07-28 ground). asset_nodes carries submitted_by and approved_by as TEXT while 0 of 95 rows have auth_uid at all, and the table has 0 audit triggers. So an approval - the governance act the whole queue exists for - is attributed to a typed NAME, recorded nowhere the database can vouch for, and performed on rows nobody is provably the author of. Distinct from PMK3, which covered a COMPLETION's tamper-evidence: this is the DECISION itself, plus the forgeable-name half PMK3 never had to face because pm_completions has a real auth_uid. REFINED BY THE AH3 WALK, which is what a walk is for. The premise was half wrong and the correction is worth more than the guess: the approval ACT is NOT ungoverned - wh_guard_supervisor_approval enforces it at the database across six tables. What was missing was the OTHER outcome. Approving and refusing are the same authority exercised two ways, and the guard recognised only the first, so a submitter could reject their own work and write the reviewer's explanation. Fixed + gated (see AH03). SWEEP PARTIAL - two halves of the original premise remain and are stated rather than quietly closed: (1) submitted_by and approved_by are still TEXT names, not identity FKs, so attribution is forgeable even where the ACT is now gated; (2) asset_nodes / rcm_strategies / rcm_fmea_modes still carry 0 audit triggers across 567 rows, so an approval decision leaves no database record - the PMK3 shape on a governance act rather than a completion. SWEEP CLOSED 2026-07-28, and BOTH remaining halves turned out differently than the class premise said - which is the second time this arc a walk corrected it, and the corrections are the value. HALF ONE, THE NAMES: the premise was that submitted_by and approved_by are forgeable TEXT. They are NOT. bind_asset_nodes_submitter (BEFORE INSERT) sets auth_uid := auth.uid() and overwrites worker_name and submitted_by from hive_members; bind_approved_by_from_hive overwrites approved_by from the session whenever it changes. Caught by accident: a probe deliberately wrote approved_by='Someone Else' and the row came back 'Leandro Marquez'. So the platform already binds identity server-side on both. The SUBTLETY worth keeping, and why 20260728000013 was still needed: bind_approved_by_from_hive only fires when approved_by CHANGES. In AH3's hole the worker rejected by setting status + rejection_reason ALONE, leaving approved_by untouched - so the binding trigger had nothing to bind and the row showed a rejection with no approver and a worker-written reason. Server-side name-binding does not cover a field the attacker simply does not touch. HALF TWO, THE RECORD: this one was real. 83 asset_nodes sat in a decided state and ZERO decisions were recorded - the 11 approve/reject rows in hive_audit_log were all CLIENT-written and none were for assets. A client-written row is skipped by any write that bypasses the page, which AH3 proved reachable. Closed by migration 20260728000015: an AFTER UPDATE trigger firing only on a transition INTO a reviewer state, recording status_was/now, the rejection_reason, submitted_by, the claimed approved_by AND the identity resolved from auth.uid() - kept as separate fields so a mismatch between the claimed approver and the actual writer is visible rather than silently reconciled. Scoped so an ordinary edit to an approved asset stays out of the trail, keeping it readable enough to audit. Proven: a location edit logs 0 rows, the reject decision logs 1 with the full picture. THE CLASS AS IT NOW STANDS: a governance decision needs (a) an identity bound where the write lands - already true here, (b) an authority check covering EVERY outcome, not just approval - fixed in AH3, and (c) a database record of the decision itself - fixed here. Gated by tools/validate_approval_authority.py, now 6 checks; teeth proven by dropping the audit trigger (exit 1) and against the real pre-fix guard (3 of 4 fail).

AHK2.name: A number that sets inspection timing must be FALSIFIABLE
AHK2.notes: OPEN on measured evidence. Weibull beta/eta, the P-F interval and FMEA RPN each DECIDE WHEN A MACHINE IS NEXT OPENED UP - they do not report history, they set future action, so being wrong is physical rather than cosmetic. Ground measured 172 RCM strategies and 300 FMEA modes, all approved, computed by edge functions (weibull-fitter, pf-calculator) with no in-repo oracle found. Each needs a stated method, a REFUSAL path when the data cannot support the fit, and a checkable oracle. Distinct from PMK1: that was a metric flattering what was DONE; this is a computed value deciding what happens NEXT. REFINED BY THE AH9 WALK. The premise was that these numbers might be produced without a refusal path; the measurement says otherwise and the correction is the finding. Weibull HAS a well-designed refusal (MIN_FAILURES_FOR_FIT=4, no fit attempted, an actionable diagnostic) and it is the honest kind - it declines rather than guessing. What was broken is the DURABILITY of the refusal's reason: computed, returned once, never stored, so the explanation was blank on every page load after the first. A calculation that refuses is only as useful as the sentence that survives with it. SWEEP PARTIAL, stated rather than quietly closed: the P-F interval calculator (pf_intervals, 91 rows) has the same shape and is UNWALKED - whether it refuses on thin data, and whether ITS reason persists, is AH10 and the next slice. FMEA RPN (300 modes) is arithmetic on three 1-10 inputs and needs a different question - whether the inputs are defensible, not whether the product is. SWEEP CLOSED by AH10 across both computed numbers. Weibull: refuses well AND its reason now persists (fixed + gated). P-F: refuses well and communicates at compute time, but its reason cannot persist because pf_days is NOT NULL - measured, and deliberately left that way rather than weakening the column that guarantees every stored P-F row has a real window. The class's rule stands with a caveat worth keeping: a refusal's reason should persist WHERE A ROW EXISTS TO CARRY IT; where the schema legitimately forbids the row, the refusal must at least be unmistakable at the moment it happens, which P-F does. RPN is arithmetic on human 1-10 inputs and belongs to a different question (are the inputs defensible), noted on AH07.

AHK3.name: The fixture must contain every state the workflow can be in
AHK3.notes: EARNED BY THE AH2 WALK 2026-07-28, and it earned itself by BLOCKING one. RULE: a workflow state with no rows is a state nobody has walked, so the seeder is part of the test surface - and the failure is quiet, because a fixture missing a STATE looks exactly like a fixture that is fine. EVIDENCE: asset_nodes had 95 rows, ALL status='approved', 0 pending, 0 rejected, 0 with auth_uid. Every affordance built for the other states - the pending queue, the rejection reason, the restore path - was unreachable, which is why the PDDA arc's F21 (a worker's Pending-assets tile always reads 0) sat undiagnosed: there had never been a pending asset to see. The hole in AH3 had been sitting behind that same gap. SHARPENS LB13/LB17 from missing RELATIONSHIPS to missing STATES. FIX: the seeder now generates status and its companion fields together (_governance_state), so the states exist AND cannot be internally incoherent. SWEEP PARTIAL: rcm_strategies is still 172 approved / 0 unapproved, so the strategy approval gate remains unwalkable - that is AH8's fixture and the next slice. GATE TODO: a check that each governed table holds >0 rows in every non-terminal state it defines. SWEEP CLOSED by AH8: rcm_strategies now carries its non-terminal state (146/26) and the strategy->PM link has both branches (21 linked / 151 cold-start). Three tables were missing a state for three DIFFERENT reasons - asset_nodes because a seeder hand-off dropped the field, rcm_strategies because an approval flag was unconditional, and the PM link because the empty state was DELIBERATE and nobody had seeded its counterpart. The last is the subtle one: a documented, correct disposition can still leave a branch undemonstrable, and the answer is a SAMPLE rather than overriding the disposition.
